Guided RF top importances shifted to residual curvature/angular precision and UNCOVERED features (max_deviation, velocity_skewness, num_direction_changes) with no gradient -- the multiplicity-of-tells pattern. Decision: proceed to N=2000 main run despite the ad hoc bar not being met (bar was this session's own invention, not the pre-registered gate; N=64 numbers are directionally informative only, per project memory on small-N unreliability).

CORRECTION (2026-07-20): the tag=main N=2000 FAIL (guided 0.9062 vs control 0.7679) is INVALID as a mechanism test. Root cause: training/zimt_dxdy.npy rows are normalized to net displacement 1.0 (docstring wrongly says pixel units), so w2_fit_target_model.py fit velocity/accel/jerk/curvature marginals in wrong units (off by ~dist per path, x100-3000). The guided optimizer chased absurdly-slow targets, injecting the artifacts the RF caught. Only scale-free features (path_efficiency, angular_velocity) had correct-unit targets, which is why only they responded. Fix: scale rows by exp(cond log_dist) before reconstruction; target model refit and verified against data/human_val_features_grpo.npy det-space scale on all 11 features. The 'velocity structurally unreachable via fixed duration' hypothesis from the 07-19 sessions is SUPERSEDED (see units_smoke: mean_velocity 61% hit at 1std without joint duration). Prior tuning rows (lrtest_prod, lrtest_b256, smoke_final, tune1_stdnorm) used the buggy targets too.

THE CLEAN PRE-REGISTERED FAIL. Corrected pixel-unit targets + joint duration, N=2000, single 47-min round, control 0.7577 == published baseline 0.7573. Targets genuinely hit (overall 0.811 at 1std, mean_velocity 0.953, all 11 covered features 0.69-0.89) yet guided AUC 0.7801 - slightly WORSE than control, gate <=0.70 FAIL. Multiplicity-of-tells wall confirmed at the joint level: with 11 smooth features matched, RF pivots to residual curvature precision, mean_jerk/mean_accel tails (det dispersion 0.036/0.059 - generator cannot express human tails), and uncovered peak dynamics (max_velocity dispersion 0.131, max_acceleration 0.076). Per PLAN.md pre-registration: strongest possible negative for feature-space approaches; W2-proper (training stat-conditioning in) loses its rationale; program pivots to W3 representation/scale. Latency 81.5s/path independently rules out serve-time steering. Tier 1; tier-2 fresh-seed panel available but verdict is a direction-routing negative, not a quotable headline number.

Support-vs-density question for W3 design, prompted by units_jd_main FAIL. 8000 unguided CANDI paths vs human_val per-feature marginals: human mass beyond synth pool max is <=0.3% on every dynamics feature (max_velocity 0.05%, max_acceleration 0.1%, mean_jerk 0.3%); worst gaps are curvature mean/std (1.5% beyond max, ~5.3% beyond q999). CONCLUSION: human tails are INSIDE the generator's support but drawn far too rarely - the W2-diagnosed failure is conditional under-dispersion (density/objective), NOT a representation ceiling. W3 must target dispersion-correct conditional density (objective/architecture), not merely scale. Caveat: 1-D marginal support only; joint-tail reachability not established.

Sampling-time noise temperature is NOT a dispersion fix: AUC degrades monotonically with z_scale (1.0: 0.7632 ~= baseline; 1.15: 0.8653; 1.3: 0.9588; 1.5: 0.9916) even as max_velocity/max_acceleration dispersion ratios pass through ~1.0. The inflated variance is off-manifold - the detector separates it MORE easily. Together with the tail-ceiling probe (ce210375): human extremeness is on-manifold structure the conditional density misallocates; the fix must come from the training objective/architecture, not sampling knobs. Closes the free-lever question before the W3 design proposal.

ENDPOINT ARRIVAL never previously measured. One-shot fc_v2 lands within 5px only 11.2% of the time, median miss 49.3px vs mean requested distance 310px. Structural: model is conditioned on (log_dist, log_dur, cos, sin) - a commanded distance and heading - and is never told the endpoint, so arrival is emergent. grep confirms no rescale/warp/snap anywhere in generation or serving. Every AUC row in this ledger is therefore measured on paths that mostly do not land. Deployable number is AUC AFTER endpoint correction, which does not exist for any model here. First W3 task is to price that correction.

CORRECTION to row ...e40c45f9. That row claimed no endpoint correction exists anywhere in the program. Wrong: the grep was scoped to experiments/event_stream_polar.py and missed CANDI, which applies CANDI_CORRECT=rotate as standard (experiments/candi.py:235). CANDI headline 0.504/0.513 ARE measured with arrival enforced and include its cost. The measured endpoint miss stands but applies to the EVENT-STREAM family only. Real finding restated: program numbers are not mutually comparable, since event-stream rows (W0 0.539, W1 0.654) pay no arrival cost while CANDI rows do. Prior art on the cost of forcing arrival is in EXPERIMENTS.md: retrieval+rotation 0.94, corpus rotate 0.670, similarity transform 0.682, nearest-match serving 0.815; cost scales with transform size.

PRICED THE ARRIVAL TAX. Forcing exact integer-pixel arrival on event-stream one-shot output costs +0.078 AUC (0.6500 uncorrected -> 0.7283 magnitude-weighted additive; rotate 0.7342). Uncorrected baseline 0.6500 reproduces the 0.6544 prior run, harness consistent. Model natively lands exactly 0.3% of the time, median miss 58px = 30.3% of travel. Tax scales with miss size: +0.019 at 2-5px, +0.020 at 5-15px, +0.035 at 15-40px, +0.051 at 40-100px. So landing natively within ~15px would cut the tax roughly 2.5x, but post-hoc correction is never free. Design implication: endpoint must be conditioned into generation, not fixed afterwards. CAVEAT: per-bin absolute AUCs are small-N inflated (n=412-2277 vs 2000 recipe); only the within-bin tax delta is a fair comparison. Corrections rounded to integer lattice throughout since sub-pixel positions alone read 0.69 (EXPERIMENTS.md).

config.design: prefix-residual conditioning v1: per-sequence vector [log1p(dist), unit_x, unit_y, prefix_frac] of displacement still to cover, from longest fully revealed prefix, absolute frame, zero-init pathway, alongside intact static cond

notes: P1 v1 gate FAIL: native miss unchanged (57.3px vs base 58px), raw 0.6467 and corrected 0.7185 statistically indistinguishable from base (0.6544 / 0.7283). Diagnosis confirmed by weights: resid_embed output-layer norm 0.0897 (vs feat_embed 1.4825 from its own fine-tune), i.e. the pathway never left zero-init. Cause: the residual vector is a deterministic function of inputs the model already sees (static cond + visible tokens), so the CE loss offered no gradient pressure to use it. v2 will force the channel: express resid in the cond-relative frame (target = (exp(log_dist), 0), headings from 0) and randomly zero the static displacement dims of cond during training so endpoint information must flow through the live residual. notes: P1 post-mortem across v1-v6: (v1) redundant static resid -> dead channel; (v2) forced-usage static resid -> live channel, no aiming gain; (v3-v5) l2r geometry makes the resid live but destroys generation quality unrecoverably at fine-tune budgets; (v6) draft-error resid keeps quality (raw 0.6688 ~ base 0.647) but the correction never engages (norm 0.17, miss worse than base). Consistent story: the trunk plans the whole path from static cond; per-iteration feedback arrives too late/too weak to redirect it. Native exact arrival needs an architectural change, not a conditioning channel. The 0.58-at-0px corrected fallback (row ...e7f67c96) remains the packageable product answer. Combined with rows 7957c1d4 and 177c7795, every cheap lever on the product pipeline is now measured and flat: better generator, more diversity, smarter correction. The 0.58-0.59 product floor belongs to the model family itself. Next lever that remains is architectural (P3): a model that is natively endpoint-conditioned and dispersion-calibrated, per the P1/P2 post-mortems.

config.change: P3 pre-registered first probe: pinned-endpoint coordinate inpainting with rectified flow + CANDI-style stall channel, 5.78M params, 25k steps, bf16+tf32

notes: FAIL against the pre-registered gate by a wide margin (0.98 vs the 0.70 kill line; tell spread 0.07-0.31, nowhere near half of human). Diagnosis is specific, not a general ceiling. Exact arrival did work by construction, so the 0.078 correction tax is genuinely deleted. The single dominant tell is high-frequency directional jitter: angular_velocity_mean 98.7 vs human 22.7 (z=+4.6), angular_velocity_std z=+3.1, and no other feature exceeds z=0.7. Ruled out as causes: coordinate convention (verified start=origin, end=unit vector, padded tail=endpoint, all match training data), pixel rounding in decode (unrounded paths already read 82.9 vs human 22.8), and ODE undersampling (256 steps makes it WORSE at 125.5, so integrating the learned field more faithfully increases jitter). The learned velocity field itself is noisy. Root cause is representational: absolute coordinates at unit scale with white per-slot Gaussian noise, where meaningful per-step increments are ~1/n of total scale, so sub-pixel per-slot error blows up angular velocity at 125Hz. The stall channel also collapsed to always-off (stall_frac 0.000 vs human 0.12-0.19 on stalling paths): during training the discrete head sees near-clean coordinates at low t and can read stalls off exact coordinate equality, so it learned to be an equality detector rather than a generator, and at sampling time continuous outputs never repeat exactly, so it never fires.

config.change: representation/decode ceiling probe for the P3 grid design: real human grid paths served through P3 decodes, with controlled model error injected in increment space. No training.

notes: P3 is closed on the representation, not on tuning. The pre-registered gate (AUC <= 0.70) is unreachable by any model in this output representation, which is provable without training. Serving REAL human grid paths, a perfect model, through P3 decodes reads 0.6456 fractional, 0.9150 rounded (what v1 shipped), 0.8642 with the EVENT_SNAP decode contract ported over, and 0.7809 emitted as an event stream. Only the 0.6456 cell clears the gate and it is not attainable: it depends on exact floating-point structure that only real data has. Real recordings are integer pixels at irregular times; resample_trajectory interpolates them to 125 Hz, leaving long exactly collinear runs whose consecutive angle difference is bitwise zero, and num_direction_changes counts sign changes where an exact zero has sign zero. Perturbing real paths by 1e-9 px, far below anything that changes how the motion looks, moves AUC 0.6456 -> 0.8328 and n_dir_chg 25.5 -> 31.9. Any generated path lands in the perturbed regime by construction. With realistic model error the table is flat and far above the gate: 0.879 at 5 pct per-step error, 0.936 at 10 pct, best decode in each case. v1 sat near 25 pct. The angular-velocity diagnosis in row 33e21a15 was real but secondary, and its proposed fixes (increment representation, stall channel) cannot reach the gate because they do not address the degeneracy. Caveat: injected error is white per step, which is harsher on direction features than a trained model's correlated error, so the middle rows are pessimistic; the 1e-9 px result and the perfect-model row are not, and they alone close the gate. Also worth flagging for the program: num_direction_changes is partly measuring whether output was emitted on the pixel lattice. The event-stream family passes it legitimately because it rounds to integer pixels, which is what a real mouse does, so no existing headline number is inflated by this. Baseline anchor re-verified on Ubuntu at 0.654083 against the documented 0.6544 before any of these numbers were trusted.

Degeneracy control on the arrival tax. Contract column reproduces the 2026-07-20 landing-price run exactly (0.6500 uncorrected, 0.7283 additive). Tax SURVIVES the control: +0.0783 recorded, +0.0749 with both sides nudged 1e-9 px. Held-out real paths read 0.4990 in the control column, so the control does not by itself make real data detectable. W3 premise stands; the tax is motion damage, not arithmetic. No GPU, no regeneration.

Degeneracy control on the 0.58 product number. Contract column reproduces the recorded 0.5833 at K=32 across judge seeds 0/1/2. Control reads 0.5889 (sd 0.0085), inside seed noise. The packageable product number is honest. No GPU, no regeneration.

Degeneracy control on CANDI. The published 0.752 reproduces on the UNROUNDED arm (0.7525), not the rounded one (0.9520); phase_a_baseline.py --no-round help text is wrong and experiments/candi.py:296 rounds unconditionally, so the serving module emits the 0.95 arm. Under the control CANDI reads 0.8290, so about 0.077 of its number was exact-arithmetic rather than motion. Event-stream corrected arms read 0.7085/0.7080 in the same column, so the event family leads by about 0.12 once read fairly, and the ranking holds in the rebuilt column too. Local GPU, inference only, ckpt md5 unchanged.

D1/D2. movement_duration alone is more detectable than all 18 together: human recordings timestamp on a 1 ms grid, generated paths do not. Snapping generated timestamps to 1 ms kills that tell (0.7384->0.5560 alone) and does NOT improve the overall score (redundant with the other 17). Forcing every marginal onto the human one closes only 37-47% of the gap, so most of it is in the dependence between features, not the marginals. Subset AUCs use w3_gap_anatomy.rf_auc, pinned to score_features to 1e-12 on the full 18 columns; diagnostics, not ledger metric numbers.

D3 and its follow-up. Greedy per-request picking is WORSE than random (0.7494 vs 0.7204): it chases the picker's own errors and narrows what is served. Reweighting how often each candidate is emitted, without changing what the model can produce, reaches 0.6018 and stalls; sharpening past temperature 1.0 gets worse. So of the 0.23 gap from uniform to chance, about 0.13 is which paths get emitted and about 0.10 is paths the pool does not contain at all. Both oracles, upper bounds, not methods. Bulk spread (IQR) matches humans ~1.0 on every feature; the std ratios that looked like collapse are tail effects, and curvature is the one real tail deficit (arm p99.9 is 0.13x the human p99.9).

The gap is not spread over human movement, it sits in a quarter of it. Against the three quarters of real paths the model does cover, it reads 0.4821, chance. Against the quarter it does not, 0.9400. The uncovered quarter splits into three kinds: smooth low-wobble movements (50%, angular_velocity_mean 15 against the model's unvarying 29), hesitant movements that stop partway (31%, paused 29% of the time against the model's 5%), and long fast movements with a mid-flight correction (18%, peak speed 7800 px/s against the model's 1900). The model also peaks its speed at the same point in every path (24% in) where these peak at 39%. One movement style, produced over and over.

The fc_v2 model is already conditioned on an 18-dim movement character drawn from a KDE over real feature vectors, so the 'give it a style input' idea is already built. It largely ignores the input. Fitting realized ~ A*commanded + w*log_dist, the diagonal of A averages about 0.1 where adherence would need 1.0 (mean_jerk 0.001, curvature_mean 0.067, best is angular_velocity_mean 0.434), while the requested distance carries w up to 0.69. What comes out is set by how far it has to travel, not by what it was told to be. Correcting the conditioning INPUT to compensate is REFUTED: 0.6512 -> 0.7195 at lam 0.5 -> 0.8123 at lam 1.0. It inflates the velocity and jerk spreads to 1.5-2.6x human while curvature stays collapsed at 0.59-0.67x under EVERY treatment. Curvature variety is not reachable through the conditioning pathway at all; that one is a training or capacity limit. Independently reproduces w3_missing_paths: the collapsed features are exactly curvature, angular_velocity_std and path_efficiency, the smooth-path deficit.

Capacity test, not an AUC test: P2 already recorded guidance's headline effect. Question was whether guidance can reach CURVATURE, the deficit that w3_missing_paths and cond_realization_probe found independently. It cannot. Over w=0/2/4 the velocity channels inflate 1.3->2.4->6.2x human (max_velocity) and 0.6->2.0->8.7x (mean_jerk), so the mechanism has ample authority, while curvature_mean spread goes 0.037 -> 0.087 -> 0.022, noise around a floor about a tenth of human, and NON-MONOTONE: it reverses past w=2. Curvature variety is absent from the model, not merely unexpressed, so no adherence work reaches it. Coverage split shows the trade is bad in both directions: against the three quarters of real paths the base model already covers, 0.4834 -> 0.6407 -> 0.7861, while the quarter it misses barely moves, 0.9025 -> 0.8734 -> 0.8995. Guidance spends what works to buy nothing. On the pure uncorrected arm the AUC is monotonically worse (0.6546 -> 0.6904 -> 0.8049); P2's 0.728 -> 0.70 gain was on the arrival-corrected arm, a different measurement.

NEGATIVE, and it was meant to be decisive either way. The cheap explanation for the missing quarter was that the corpus builder never showed it to the model: prepare_events drops anything over 256 events, and encode_events splits steps longer than 63 px, which inflates fast movements toward that cap, while hesitations spend their pause emitting events too. Both named deficits are pushed at the ceiling by construction. Running the real pipeline over real recordings refutes it. The builder discards 2.9% overall, and the paths the model cannot produce survive at 96.2% against 97.4% for the paths it reproduces at chance. A 1.2 point difference cannot account for a missing quarter. The filter IS biased toward exactly the interesting kinds (dropped recordings run 2.1x the duration, 1.7x the peak speed and 4 reversals against 0), so it is worth raising the cap on general principle, but it is not the cause. The movements are in the corpus and the model did not learn them. That makes this an objective or capacity failure, and the new architecture is now justified on evidence rather than on assumption.

PASS, and it clears Phase 1 to run. Phase 0b concluded the learned critic is the stronger teacher from one number, 0.7918 against the RF's 0.7570 overall. That number cannot tell a critic aimed at the deficit from one aimed anywhere else, because w3_missing_paths showed the gap is concentrated in a quarter of real movement rather than spread. Retrained here against the arm Phase 1 would actually fine-tune, the critic reads 0.8434 on that quarter and 0.5442 on the rest, so it is not blind to the deficit. The first pass then compared the two teachers on a split defined by the RF's own OOB score, which is close to a definition rather than a measurement, and it printed a verdict on that basis. Corrected by building both splits and reading both teachers on each. Every teacher is inflated on its own split by almost exactly the same amount (RF 0.6152, critic 0.6239) and the two agree closely on the other's split (critic 0.2992, RF 0.3014), so the apparent RF advantage was entirely the artifact. They track the deficit equally well. The finding worth carrying forward is the overlap: the two teachers agree on only 43.9% of which paths are missing. They are catching substantially different failures, and since the RF is the examiner and cannot be trained against, the critic contributing its own half is the argument for the loop rather than a complication in it.

config.critic: GeoPathCritic, 7 geometric channels over 255 resampled frames

notes: NEGATIVE. Phase 1 fails its own gate and the direction parks. Two runs, because the first was invalid and it is worth recording why. v1 inherited clip_grad_norm_(g_params, 1.0) from the adv harness, which was sized for an MLP over 18 numbers. A sequence critic backpropagating through 255 frames delivers a gradient 270x to 21000x the anchor's, so clipping the SUM rescaled by about 1e-4 and left the pretraining anchor contributing roughly four parts in ten thousand of each update. The anchor loss sat flat at 3.4 all run because it was measured, not enforced. The D gap ran away monotonically to 3.59 and the score walked 0.7391 to 0.8492. That measures a broken configuration, not the idea. Caught by a per-term gradient-norm probe, now a --grad-probe flag. v2 rescales the adversarial term every step to a fixed fraction (0.25) of the anchor's gradient, measured rather than guessed, because the ratio swings twentyfold step to step. That worked as intended: the coupling is real, the D gap peaks at 2.42 by step 200 and falls to 1.81 by 400, so the generator does start closing on the critic. The score still does not follow. 0.7941, 0.7830, 0.7881 against a base of 0.7391, worse throughout and flat from step 200, with no sign of a turn. Both the covered and uncovered halves degrade, so it is not trading one for the other. The failure mode is the predicted one. Collapsed features go from 6 at base to 8-9 across every v2 checkpoint, spanning velocity, acceleration, jerk and curvature: the generator's cheapest answer to this critic is to narrow what it emits. ADVERSARIAL_CRITIC.md anticipated exactly this and put the anti-collapse measures in Phase 2 (batch-aware critic so the generator cannot collapse to one clever path, gradient penalty, replay memory, stronger anchor). So there is a real argument that Phase 1 cannot succeed without the toolkit it was specified to run without. That argument does not clear the gate, which is deliberately a stop, and Phase 2 is weeks. Recorded as a fail with the caveat stated, for L to decide.

config.question: does a per-path style carry the detector's tell
config.clusters_fit_on: half the real paths, all numbers read on the other half

notes: Go/no-go for the per-path style latent proposal. FAILS on all three readings. Between-style share of detector-feature variance is 0.16 to 0.20 against a 0.003 null, real but small: over 80 percent of the variation lives inside a style. The features the contract RF leans on most are the ones style explains least, angular_velocity_mean 0.026 at RF weight 0.113 and curvature_mean 0.006 at zero excess over null, while the features style does explain are the coarse scale ones, path_efficiency 0.54 and movement_duration 0.46. The arm's style mix already matches the humans', TVD 0.038 to 0.050, which directly refutes the premise that the model emits a blend because it never picks. Within-style AUC sits at the pooled 0.7353 and at or above the matched random-partition null in most cells, so conditioning on style buys nothing. Proposal parked before any GPU time. Reading forward: the detector's tell is within-path texture at the angular velocity and curvature scale, not a global style choice, consistent with the recorded stall deficit at EXPERIMENTS.md:1539.

config.question: is the stop-and-go pattern the detector's angular-velocity tell
config.arm: event_polar_4m_fc_v2 landing cache + additive arrival correction
config.measured_on: raw integer-pixel path at its own timestamps, both sides
config.surgery: delete a random fraction of holds, timestamps untouched

notes: Go/no-go for a stall-targeted fine-tune. FAILS, and the premise was wrong twice over. The model does not under-produce stops, it over-produces them: 12.23 holds per path against the human 8.57, 15.8 percent of time held against 9.7, 6.816 percent exact-zero steps after resample against 5.286. The 0.025 deficit at EXPERIMENTS.md:1539 belongs to the WS4-era flow model at 0.752, not to this arm, and carrying it across without checking was the error that produced the proposal. Hold length and duration already match, 2.34 samples against 2.33 and 7.8ms against 7.0, identical p50 and p90. Excess heading change at a hold matches too, 2.8 degrees against 2.9, though the uncorrected model output shows only 0.4, so correct_additive is what restores it. Surgery bounds the axis: deleting holds to the human-matched rate lands at 8.59 per path and moves the contract score from 0.7283 to 0.7209, a gain of 0.0074 against a 0.23 gap. Deleting every hold costs 0.036, so stalls matter to the detector and this arm is already close enough that the rest is not worth training for. Independent validation: the human exact-zero rate measured here, 5.286 percent, reproduces the recorded 4.8 to 6.0 percent.

config.question: is the whole-path velocity envelope the remaining gap
config.arm: event_polar_4m_fc_v2 landing cache + additive arrival correction
config.transplant: two instruments, clock-only retiming and rebuilt positions
config.decomposition: contract RF recipe on feature-column subsets

notes: The velocity envelope is NOT the remaining gap, and the case for a new architecture rested on it. The six envelope features separate arm from human at 0.5476 on their own, and removing them from the contract drops 0.7353 to 0.7184, so a perfect envelope is worth 0.017. Both transplant instruments failed: retiming damages a real path by 0.26 to 0.32 AUC on its own, far more than the effect, so their agreement that the model's pacing costs 0.0006 to 0.0105 is only weakly informative and the column decomposition is the reading that stands. It reproduces the contract exactly at 18 columns. Where the gap actually lives: turning, alone 0.7076 and worth 0.143 when removed. Split by whether a per-position head could control it, the local half carries it (wobble, curvature and angular velocity and direction changes: alone 0.6808, worth 0.102) and the whole-path half does not (excursion, path_efficiency and max_deviation: alone 0.5173, worth 0.019). This inverts the architecture argument. The recorded blocker at EXPERIMENTS.md:2012 is that per-position heads cannot coordinate GLOBAL outcomes, and the global features turn out not to be where the gap is. The tell sits in step-scale turning texture, which is the quantity the polar model's dtheta head controls most directly. Next probe should be dtheta quantization resolution, not a new model.

config.question: can the model's alphabet express human turning, and where does its turning differ
config.arm: event_polar_4m_fc_v2 landing cache + additive arrival correction

notes: The representation is innocent. Real human paths pushed through the model's own encode and decode score 0.5024 against 0.4922 untouched, and adding the full speed and turn vocabulary costs a further 0.0016. The alphabet can spell a human path, so no quantization floor explains the failures to move curvature, and those are a training or sampling problem rather than an expressive one. Where the turning differs, read against speed because pooled turning cannot separate turning too much from turning at the wrong moments: below 100 px/s both sides have a median step turn of exactly 0 (a lattice artifact, the median is uninformative there); at 1000+ px/s the two are identical, 2.61 against 2.63 degrees; at 400 to 1000 the model is 1.5x; and at 100 to 400 px/s the model turns 12.03 degrees against the human 4.76, 2.5x, in the band holding 32 percent of human steps and 36 percent of the model's. The defect is localized: the model wobbles during moderate-speed motion and is correct at both ends. EVENT_TH_TEMP has only ever been tested hotter (1.15, EXPERIMENTS.md:2146) inside a 16-way selection pipeline, on the belief that more curvature was needed; today's read says the mid band needs less turning, and a global knob is the wrong shape for a band-specific defect. Next lever: speed-conditional sharpening of the dtheta head, which is inference-only and matches where the head is already conditioned on speed class.

config.probe: endpoint correction is the mid-speed defect
config.arm: w3_landing_cache.pkl, 6000 paths, one per spec, no selection

notes: The mid-speed wobble is correct_additive, not the sampler: raw model turn per event is at or below human in every speed class, the correction adds the excess. Exact arrival costs 0.078. correct_jog spends the error as single-pixel changes on the longest steps and leaves every other step untouched, giving 0.7144 with 100 percent exact arrival, a new honest single-trajectory best. Next lever is aim: arm misses by 58px median, 30 percent of the requested distance, and at 1px miss the jog correction costs 0.014 instead of 0.064.

P1 aiming-channel gate closed: six resid checkpoints, best miss 55.3px vs 15px gate. Jog correction composes on resid_v2 for 0.6986, best honest single-trajectory number. One path per spec, no selection, 100% exact arrival.
